Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old male with known asthma presents with 3 hours of chest tightness, mild dyspnea, wheeze, and nonproductive cough after recent URI; currently out of inhalers. Plan: refill inhalers, short course of oral steroids, provide spacer, and safety-net advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute chest tightness for ~3 hours.
- Associated symptoms: Mild shortness of breath, wheeze, nonproductive cough; recent cold last week with sore throat and runny nose (improved), cough persisting; cough slightly worse at night but generally constant.
- Pertinent negatives: No chest pain (tightness only); not short of breath at rest; no sputum production.
- Past medical history: Asthma; allergic rhinitis/hay fever; dust allergy; childhood eczema; childhood milk protein allergy. Prior severe asthma exacerbation requiring intubation in high school (age ~16–17).
- Medications: Ventolin (salbutamol) inhaler—ran out 1 week ago; Clenil (beclomethasone) inhaler—ran out 1 week ago. Doses/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Mother with eczema; father with asthma.
- Social/preventive: Was away at university last week and forgot/refilled inhalers late.

Examination:
- 

Impression:
- Acute asthma exacerbation, likely triggered by recent viral URI and lapse in controller/rescue inhalers.

Plan:
- Prescriptions:
  - Ventolin (salbutamol) inhaler for PRN relief; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Clenil (beclomethasone) inhaler for maintenance; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Oral steroids: “2 tablets in the morning for 5 days” (drug and tablet strength not documented).
  - Spacer to optimize inhaler delivery; instructions to be provided.
- Advice:
  - Use rescue inhaler as needed; if needing Ventolin more frequently than every 3 hours, seek medical attention.
  - Seek urgent care for any deterioration: worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness/pain, light-headedness, or other concerning symptoms.
  - Rest; time off work advised (patient can self-certify for first 7 days).
- Logistics: Prescriptions to be sent within the hour.
- Follow-up: Not explicitly arranged; seek medical review if symptoms persist/worsen or increased reliever use as above.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals, oxygen saturation, peak flow, lung exam, inhaler doses/frequencies, specific oral steroid name and dose, smoking status, vaccination status (e.g., influenza), inhaler technique review beyond brief spacer mention, written asthma action plan, scheduled follow-up appointment.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Minor audio dropouts; overall information adequate.
